Title: Quinti Septimii Florentis Tertulliani quae supersunt omnia, Tomus II: libros polemicos et dogmaticos
Creator: Tertullian (Quintus Septimius Florens Tertullianus, c. 160-c. 225); Franciscus (Franz) Oehler (editor)
Publisher: Leipzig: T. O. Weigel, 1853 (title page MDCCCLIII, as read in the OCR)
Publication Date: 1853
Rights: Public Domain (pre-1930 publication); the item record's possible-copyright-status is NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT
Language: lat
Source: Internet Archive item quaesupersuntom00oehlgoog, full-text OCR file quaesupersuntom00oehlgoog_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the library/source-research thread (Claude), 2026-09-29. The item record marks possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT (Google scan, contributor Harvard University); its description lists the three tomes: T. 1 libros apologeticos et qui ad ritus et mores Christianorum pertinent, T. 2 libros polemicos et dogmaticos, T. 3 dissertationes. Title page read in the OCR: 'QUAE SUPERSUNT OMNIA EDIDIT FRANCISCUS OEHLER ... CONTINENS LIBROS POLEMICOS ET DOGMATICOS LIPSIAE T. O. WEIGEL'; the year numerals are OCR-garbled (MDCCCLIII read as MDGCGLIT).
Provenance note: Header prepended by the library thread; the OCR text follows unchanged, apart from this header. Rights basis: the printed date (1853, from the item record and the garbled-but-legible title-page numerals) clears this registry's public-domain-by-date rule; the host's NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT tag agrees. The Google boilerplate pages at the head of the OCR are left in place. OCR artifacts, running heads, line numbers and apparatus left as found; nothing was corrected, re-spaced or retyped. Measured on the OCR before vendoring: 0 Greek-script characters.
Content note: Contents per the volume's own Index: De praescriptione haereticorum, Adversus Marcionem (5 books), Adversus Hermogenem, Adversus Valentinianos, De carne Christi, De resurrectione carnis, De anima, Adversus Praxean, Adversus Iudaeos, fragments, spurious works. An older recension than CSEL 47; it is here for the works CSEL 20/47 lack (De praescriptione, De carne Christi, Adversus Iudaeos). The scan carries no separate title page for the tome inside the running text, so the tome number rests on the OCR'd half-title and the item description.
